scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 have read_type ACTUAL.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/handling gap, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets would resolve it (SH-CS framing).

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is producing incorrect bills, driving the dispute increase.

H-AMI-FEED-FAILURE.statement: AMI register reads from the vendor (MDMS) are failing to deliver or validate correctly via H-MDMS-BILL, causing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter-read collection or the H-FIELD-BILL handoff is incomplete/degraded (e.g., understaffing per SH-FIELD), causing estimated bills and disputes.

H-TICKET-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets since August reflects a CRM categorization or baseline-definition change rather than more actual billing errors.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Among disputed bills, 1785 are on ACTUAL-read bills versus 1240 on ESTIMATED-read bills (E-01), so a majority of disputes attach to bills built from actual reads, not estimate substitutions.

The tariff_change_log query (E-02) returned zero records, showing no tariff changes were logged in billing-db for the period examined; this rules out a tariff change as a cause of the wrong bills, but it is a distinct log from the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES/billing-config) that H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE concerns.

Route-log shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts (E-03), i.e. a 7-point shortfall in completed manual reads during the dispute-surge window.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; as a stakeholder claim it is NON_AUTHORITATIVE and merely corroborates the already-recorded tool finding E-02 (tariff_change_log returned 0 records) without adding new evidentiary weight.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD attributes late manual-read routes (and resulting estimated bills) to a reader staffing shortfall since July, offering a causal story for the low route completion already seen in E-03. As a non-authoritative stakeholder claim from someone with an incentive toward contract headcount increase, it corroborates but does not independently prove the H-FIELD-READ-GAP mechanism.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times (E-06) shows the CS team is already resolving disputes well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets), so slow or inadequate response handling is not an explanation for the dispute surge.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly (E-07) shows ticket counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026, confirming a sharp ~2x jump that begins specifically in August and holds into September, with no corresponding rise in June/July. The record is a count series only; it establishes magnitude and timing of the surge but says nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but that any such change is executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this corroborates the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint rather than introducing a new rule.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) shows only 320 distinct accounts received estimated bills last cycle across 40 distinct routes, with the returned fields limited to account_id and route (no read-type or import-status data), so it does not extend E-01's ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split as the W-WI-BILLQUERY item intended. The small count (320) is also far below the ~12% shortfall implied by E-03's 9200 manual-read accounts at 0.88 completion, understating the field-read-gap mechanism's expected magnitude.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August 2026, from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to ~1200/month (Aug/Sep) (E-07).
Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter-read bills (1785) over ESTIMATED bills (1240), contrary to an estimate-substitution narrative (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion is below target (0.88 vs 0.95) in Aug-Sep 2026, a separate shortfall that does not match the dispute's read-type pattern (E-03).
Dispute response times remain well within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA across 2440 tickets), so slow handling does not explain the surge (E-06).
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-07), with disputes attaching predominantly to bills built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutions (1785 vs 1240, E-01). This pattern is consistent with a billing import validation rule change around August producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), ruling out tariff change (E-02), field manual-read gaps (E-01, E-03), and slow dispute response (E-06) as the driver.
